plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
Sell SMCI and SMH to reduce tech/semis risk.
Trim QQQI to 20% to lower concentration.
Buy XLV at 5% for defensive sector exposure.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation.
Expect lower volatility and smaller potential gains.
conservative.read: This plan aims for capital preservation with lower volatility. Target monthly return is around 1.5%. Risk is minimized by cutting leverage and reducing concentrated positions.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to small positions.
Trim SMH to reduce concentrated semis exposure.
Trim QQQI to 20% to lower income concentration.
Buy XLV at 5% for defensive sector exposure.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth potential.
Expect moderate volatility and returns.
balanced.read: This plan focuses on risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It reduces leverage and concentration while adding a defensive sector. Drawdowns are expected to be manageable.

plan: Increase exposure to AI/Software names (METU, PLTU, MSFU) to 6% each.
Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to 6% each.
Buy XLV at 5% for defensive sector exposure.
This plan aggressively pursues growth through concentration and leverage.
Expect higher potential returns and significantly larger drawdowns.
Strict stop discipline is crucial due to amplified risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets around 4% per month by increasing leverage and concentrating in high-scoring setups. It carries significantly higher risk, including amplified drawdowns and potential for rapid losses due to leverage and ETF decay.

plan: Sell all high-beta tech and leveraged ETFs to zero.
Increase QQQI to 40% for income generation.
Increase SPY to 30% for broad index exposure.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income and low drawdown.
Expect lower growth potential compared to other modes.
Distributions are variable and NAV can still decline.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% per month through distributions from QQQI and SPY. It prioritizes capital preservation and low drawdown over growth. While aiming for steady income, the Net Asset Value can still fall in market downturns.
